newsitem.title: UK: Europe LPG gains with U.S, Asian markets firm too.
newsitem.headline: Europe LPG gains with U.S, Asian markets firm too.

text.p: Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) prices were a little stronger on Friday despite mild weather in Europe, with prices buoyed by good buying in Asian markets and still-healthy prices in the U.S., traders said.
European cargo prices were stronger with offers of propane seen at around $270 a tonne cif NWE and butane prices pegged somewhere "in the mid 240s," according to one dealer.
Strength in the U.S., which saw Belvieu propane offered at 54 cents a gallon on Friday, remains a key factor in high prices in other markets.
"The U.S. is a bit perkier," one dealer said, but added that netback levels, although rising, were still not likely to provoke arbitrage trade.

U.S. propane stocks rose by 1.2 million barrels in the week ending October 18, latest data from the Energy Information Adsministration showed. But stocks remain 5.75 million barrels, or 10 percent, down from last year.
European coaster markets were very lacklustre, with propane assessed at around $260 fob NWE, almost unchanged from last week, and butane at $215/$220.
